chunks: And informed me was Al-Husayn ibn Ubaydullah, from Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawood al-Qummi, may Allah have mercy on him, from Abu Ali ibn Himam, who said:

Muhammad ibn Ali al-Shalmaghani al-Azaqari was sent to Shaykh Al-Husayn ibn Rauh to ask him to perform Mubahila, and he said: 'I am the companion of the Man (the Imam), and I have been ordered to manifest knowledge, which I have manifested inwardly and outwardly; so let me have Mubahila with you.' Shaykh (may Allah be pleased with him) sent back the reply: 'Whichever of us has his companion die first, he is the one bearing the anathema (Makhsum).' Al-Azaqari died first; he was killed and crucified, and Ibn Abi Awn was taken with him. This was in the year 323 AH.

key_terms.صاحب الرجل: Companion of the Man (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Mubahila between Al-Azaqari and Shaykh Al-Husayn ibn Rauh?
ai.summary: This account from the Minor Occultation highlights the intense scrutiny faced by the Four Deputies (al-Nuwwab al-Arba'a), specifically Shaykh Al-Husayn ibn Rauh, who served as the primary link between the hidden Imam and the community. The Mubahila event serves as a divine validation of the deputy's authority, where the premature death of Al-Azaqari's companion confirmed the truth of Ibn Rauh's claim to be the true representative of the Imam. This incident underscores the political and theological risks associated with claiming proximity to the Imam during the period of Ghayba.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 258 - It is narrated from Husain bin Ubaidullah from Abul Hasan Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Dawood Qummi from Abu Ali Ibn Himam that he said:

Muhammad Ibn Ali ­Shalmaghani Azaqari challenged Shaykh Husain Ibn Rauh to a Mubahila (imprecation contest), saying, “I am the companion of the Imam and have been ordered to manifest my knowledge, which I have manifested expressly and implicitly; so come to my Mubahila.” The Shaykh replied, “Whoever of us dies first, is the one who bears the anathema.” Azaqari died first, as he was killed, crucified and Ibn Abi Aun was taken with him. This was in the year three hundred and thirteen.
